page.layout: One column of running text. A centred heading "3. HABACUC." sits within the column. No marginal notes except one small mark at the right edge beside "Regis". Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: Det nobis Deus, ut quemadmodū in Prophetarum labores ingresi sunt Apo-stoli: fuitque miranda ἁρμονία[?] doctrinæ, quam utriusq; Testamenti Ministri magno consensu tradiderunt: ita quoque nos primum illorum, deinde & Præceptorum orthodoxorum vestigijs insiste-tes, dulcissima συμφωνίαν[?] doctrinæ diu nitus revelatæ, pro eo dono, quod nobis Deus dedit, ad Dei gloriam & Sanctorum instaurationē, studiosè & constanter profiteamur.
main_text.head: 3. HABACUC.
main_text.p: Non præcisè cōstat, quo anno prophe-tare cœperit Habacuc, cùm nulla ulliusb[?] Regis Iudæ mentio ab eo facta sit.

D. Hieronymus in Prologo ad Chromatium Episcopum, Danieli Habacucu[?] σύγχρονον[?] facit, mentione facta historiæ de illo in leonum lacum misso, ut tamen certò non pronunciet: & alibi nō obscu-re, παραλληλόμενα[?] Danieli aspersa, neget historicam habere fidem.
In libro Seder Olam, cap.20. hæc verba exstant: Ioël, Nahum & Habacuc vaticinabantur tempestate Manassis. At quo-

page.notes: Greek words (ἁρμονία, συμφωνίαν, σύγχρονον, παραλληλόμενα) are read from a small, worn type and are doubtful; the letters are marked [?]. "Habacucu" at the end of the Hieronymus sentence may carry a tilde or abbreviation mark. The small "b" beside "ullius" at the right edge is a faint mark, possibly a reference letter. The catchword "niam" is the start of the next page. The page number "6" and running head are at the top. No signature is visible.
